title: Shared controls reduced six drought slope error bounds by 18-32 percent in three bird samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We tested whether shared controls narrow error bounds for within-group bird drought magnitude slopes. We used 51 records in 17 blocks from three studies in Australia and Hawaii in a 2024 data release. The common log control cancels exactly from each slope. With local linear errors and arbitrary correlations among drought means, six upper sampling standard errors fell by 18.2-31.5 percent against a conventional ratio-error bound. Two six-test corrected normal-reference intervals were below zero. Both used the same two Swift Parrot years. Adding its third available year made the three-month interval include zero. A 1.469-fold increase in marginal variances also removed both exclusions. The other four intervals included zero. The algebra gives a useful bound reduction, but these records do not establish a repeated negative drought magnitude link. Sample identity, correct marginal errors and valid log-mean approximations are necessary assumptions. Detection bias, few weather histories, selected records and overlapping periods limit inference. Source records remain external. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, checks and a static figure are included.

display.caption: Common control cancellation reduces upper sampling standard errors by 18-32 percent. Two intervals below zero share the same two Swift Parrot years; third-year inclusion removes the three-month exclusion. Gray shows a conventional ratio-error benchmark. Blue allows arbitrary correlations among drought means after control cancellation.
